code: simulate_clusters <- function(k, d, n = 5000L) {   centers <- matrix(runif(k * d), nrow = k)   sigma <- min(dist(centers)) / 3   cluster <- rep_len(seq_len(k), n)   x <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = d)   for (j in seq_len(k)) {     rows <- which(cluster == j)     rotation <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(rnorm(d * d), nrow = d)))     shape <- diag(runif(d, 0.2, 1), nrow = d) %*% rotation     noise <- matrix(rnorm(length(rows) * d), ncol = d)     x[rows, ] <- sweep(sigma * noise %*% shape, 2L, centers[j, ], "+")   }   list(x = x, cluster = cluster) } optimal_distortion <- function(x, cluster) {   sum(vapply(     split(seq_len(nrow(x)), cluster),     \(rows) sum(scale(x[rows, , drop = FALSE], scale = FALSE)^2),     numeric(1L)   )) }  set.seed(2003) settings <- CJ(d = c(2L, 8L, 32L), k = c(5L, 20L, 80L), rep = 1:30) synthetic <- settings[,   {     sim <- simulate_clusters(k, d)     fit <- gmeans(sim$x)     .(       k_found = nrow(fit$centers),       distortion = fit$tot.withinss / optimal_distortion(sim$x, sim$cluster)     )   },   by = .(d, k, rep) ] mean_sd <- function(x, digits) {   sprintf("%.*f ± %.*f", digits, mean(x), digits, sd(x)) }  replicated <- synthetic[, title: Replicating Hamerly and Elkan (2003)
text: Figure 3 paper shows often split test makes wrong decision, function number points \(n\). type error splits one Gaussian cluster, one axis 5% shorter . type II error split two Gaussian clusters whose means \(5\sigma\) apart. paper runs 1000 tests per point.  paper, test almost never splits single Gaussian cluster, needs enough points split two clusters. paper type II error close 1 10 20 points, 0.37 50 points, 0 100 points . 0.905 30 points, 0.3 50 points, 0 100 points.
code: set.seed(2003) error_rates <- data.table(n = c(10L, 20L, 30L, 50L, 100L, 150L, 200L)) error_rates <- error_rates[,   {     type_1 <- replicate(1000L, {       x <- matrix(rnorm(2L * n), ncol = 2L) %*% diag(c(1, 0.95))       nrow(gmeans(x)$centers) > 1L     })     type_2 <- replicate(1000L, {       x <- matrix(rnorm(2L * n), ncol = 2L)       x[seq_len(n %/% 2L), 1L] <- x[seq_len(n %/% 2L), 1L] + 5       nrow(gmeans(x)$centers) == 1L     })     .(       error = c("Type I: splits one cluster", "Type II: does not split two clusters"),       rate = c(mean(type_1), mean(type_2))     )   },   by = n ] ggplot(error_rates, aes(n, rate)) +   geom_line() +   geom_point() +   facet_wrap(~error) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +   labs(x = "Number of points", y = "Error rate")

title: Anderson-Darling Normality Test — ad.test
text: Anderson-Darling test EDF omnibus test composite hypothesis normality. test statistic $$   ^2 = -n -\frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^{n} (2i - 1) [\ln(z_{}) + \ln(1 - z_{n + 1 - })] $$ \(z_{} = \Phi(\frac{x_{} - \bar{x}}{s})\). , \(\Phi\) cumulative distribution function standard normal distribution, \(\bar{x}\) \(s\) mean standard deviation data values. p-value computed modified statistic \(^2_*=^2 (1.0 + 0.75/n + 2.25/n^{2})\) according Table 4.9 Stephens (1986).

title: G-means Clustering — gmeans
text: G-means clustering algorithm extension traditional k-means algorithm automatically determines number clusters iteratively testing Gaussianity data within clusters. process begins specified initial number clusters (k_init) iteratively increases number clusters reaches specified maximum (k_max) data within clusters determined Gaussian specified significance level (level). algorithm outlined follows: Let \(C\) initial set centers (usually \(C \leftarrow \{\bar{x}\}\)). Perform k-means clustering dataset \(X\) using current set centers \(C\), .e., \(C \leftarrow \text{kmeans}(C, X)\). center \(c_j\), identify set data points \(\{x_i \mid \text{class}(x_i) = j\}\) assigned \(c_j\). Use Anderson-Darling test check set data points \(\{x_i \mid \text{class}(x_i) = j\}\) follows Gaussian distribution confidence level \(\alpha\). data points appear Gaussian, keep \(c_j\). Otherwise, replace \(c_j\) two new centers, found k-means cluster started \(c_j \pm s \sqrt{2 \lambda / \pi}\), \(s\) main principal component cluster \(\lambda\) eigenvalue. Repeat step 2 centers added.

title: Predict Method for G-means Clustering — predict.gmeans
text: predict method G-means clustering assigns new data points nearest cluster center identified G-means algorithm. method uses specified distance metric calculate distance new data point cluster centers, assigns point cluster closest center. method argument specifies distance metric use. following options: "euclidean": Euclidean distance default metric used k-means defined $$     d(x, y) = \sqrt{\sum_{=1}^{n} (x_i - y_i)^2}   $$ "manhattan": Manhattan distance defined $$     d(x, y) = \sum_{=1}^{n} |x_i - y_i|   $$ "minkowski": Minkowski distance defined $$     d(x, y) = \left( \sum_{=1}^{n} |x_i - y_i|^p \right)^{1/p},   $$ \(p\) parameter defines distance type (e.g., \(p=2\) Euclidean, \(p=1\) Manhattan).

title: gmeans (development version)
text: gmeans() now splits cluster starting two new centers along main principal component, described Hamerly Elkan (2003), instead random points. split step longer depends random seed number clusters found reliably, results may differ earlier versions. gmeans() now uses k_init = 1 default, Hamerly Elkan (2003). previous default 2 never return single cluster. one initial center result longer depends random seed. gmeans() now uses level = 0.0001 default, significance level used Hamerly Elkan (2003). previous default 0.05 often split clusters Gaussian, especially higher dimensions. gmeans() now uses k_max = Inf default, Hamerly Elkan (2003). previous default 10 silently capped number clusters data 10 clusters. gmeans() gains iter.max argument defaults 100, instead 10 used stats::kmeans(), k-means converges many clusters instead warning converge. gmeans() now stores k_init, k_max, level returned object. gmeans() now errors clearly centers passed, pointing k_init instead. gmeans() now errors clearly k_init less number rows x. New summary() method gmeans objects. New tidy(), augment(), glance() methods gmeans objects.
